PoseTracking

class PoseTracking(config, settings)[source]

Bases: object

Detect the body pose with MediaPipe, focusing on the feet.

Parameters:
configPoseTrackingConfig

MediaPipe model and parameters (KarteaHardwareService).

settingsGameSettings

Screen and calibration points used in the camera -> screen mapping.

Attributes:
settingsGameSettings

Game configuration.

pose_trackingvision.PoseLandmarker

MediaPipe Tasks pose landmarker.

feet_x, feet_yint

Screen position of the center of the feet; feet_y is locked near the bottom so the car only moves horizontally.

feet1_x, feet1_yfloat

Normalized position of the player’s left heel (landmark 30).

feet2_x, feet2_yfloat

Normalized position of the player’s right heel (landmark 29).

feet_y_freeint

Real screen y of the feet (before the lock); used by the feet marker and the feet button selection.

has_posebool

True if the player was detected in the last processed frame.

resultsPoseLandmarkerResult | None

Result of the last detection.

feet_closedbool

Kept from the original code; always False (see is_feet_closed).

last_timestamp_msint

Timestamp of the last frame sent to MediaPipe.

Notes

The frame reaches scan_feets already mirrored by Camera. MediaPipe names the sides from the body it sees, so on a mirrored image its labels are swapped: landmark 29 (“left heel”) is the player’s real right heel and 30 is the real left heel. That is why landmark 30 is used as the left foot (get_feet1) and 29 as the right foot (get_feet2).

Methods

get_feet1

Return the screen position of the first foot (landmark 30).

get_feet2

Return the screen position of the second foot (landmark 29).

get_feet_center

Return the center position of the feet (controls the car).

get_feet_marker_position

Return the real (x, y) screen position of the feet.

is_feet_closed

Reserved to detect closed feet (not implemented).

scan_feets

Detect the feet in a camera frame and annotate the image.

to_screen_position

Map a camera position to game screen coordinates.
scan_feets(image)[source]

Detect the feet in a camera frame and annotate the image.

Parameters:
imagenumpy.ndarray

Frame captured by the camera (BGR).

Returns:
numpy.ndarray

The same image, with the pose landmarks drawn when a player is detected.

Notes

  • Timestamps sent to MediaPipe (video mode) are kept strictly increasing.

  • The feet center is the midpoint of the two heels, mapped to the screen by to_screen_position; feet_y is then locked at SCREEN_HEIGHT - 50 * SCREEN_HEIGHT / BASE_HEIGHT.

  • Without a detected pose, has_pose is False and the positions keep their previous values.

get_feet_center()[source]

Return the center position of the feet (controls the car).

Returns:
tuple

(feet_x, feet_y), with feet_y locked near the bottom.

get_feet_marker_position()[source]

Return the real (x, y) screen position of the feet.

Unlike get_feet_center, y is not locked. Used by the feet marker and by the feet button selection.

Returns:
tuple[int, int] | None

(x, y) in screen pixels, or None if the player was not detected in the last frame.

get_feet1()[source]

Returns:
tuple[int, int]

Heel position mapped by to_screen_position.

get_feet2()[source]

Return the screen position of the second foot (landmark 29).

Returns:
tuple[int, int]

Heel position mapped by to_screen_position.

is_feet_closed()[source]

Reserved to detect closed feet (not implemented).

to_screen_position(x, y)[source]

Map a camera position to game screen coordinates.

Parameters:
x, yfloat

Normalized position (0-1) in the camera image.

Returns:
tuple[int, int]

Position in screen pixels.

Notes

A perspective transform maps the calibrated area (CALIBRATION_POINTS) to the control image (CONTROL_WIDTH x CONTROL_HEIGHT); the result is then scaled to the screen by WIDTH_RATIO and HEIGHT_RATIO.
